items.text: I can explain what S3 is and what 'object storage' means vs block and file storage
I understand the difference between a bucket (container) and an object (file)
I know S3 bucket names must be globally unique across all AWS accounts
I understand S3's flat namespace — no real directories, just key prefixes
I can explain S3's 11 nines durability and what it means practically
I know the S3 storage classes and when to use each (Standard, IA, Glacier tiers)
I understand S3 Versioning and how delete markers work
I can create an S3 bucket with a globally unique name in a specific region
I can upload files to an S3 bucket and view object metadata
I can confirm S3's global dashboard shows all buckets regardless of console region
I can configure a bucket for static website hosting with a public bucket policy
I can set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to IA or Glacier
I can delete all objects from a bucket and then delete the bucket
S3 is object storage, not block (EBS) or file (EFS)
Bucket names: globally unique, 3-63 chars, lowercase only
Max object size = 5 TB; Multipart Upload required for > 5 GB
S3 is a global service — all buckets visible in one dashboard
Default encryption (SSE-S3) on all new objects since January 2023
